definitions.definition: (dated) An odd, puzzling or absurd person or thing.

quote.citation: 1796, Fanny Burney, Camilla: or, A picture of youth, by the author of Evelina, page 99:
quote.text: I've always heard he was a quiz, says another, or a quoz, or some such word ; but I did not know he was such a book-worm.

quote.citation: 1833, Maria Edgeworth, Moral Tales, volume 1, page 204:
quote.text: I tell you I am going to the music shop. I trust to your honour. Lord Rawson, I know, will call me a fool for trusting to the honour of a quiz.

quote.citation: 1803, Jane Austen, chapter 7, in Northanger Abbey‎[1], published 1816:
quote.text: Where did you get that quiz of a hat? It makes you look like an old witch.

quote.citation: 1850, William Makepeace Thackeray, The History of Pendennis‎[2]:
quote.text: “I’m afraid you’re a sad quiz,” said Mrs. Bungay. ¶ “Quiz! never made a joke in my—hullo! who’s here? How d’ye do, Pendennis?

definitions.definition: (dated) One who questions or interrogates; a prying person.
A competition in the answering of questions.

quote.citation: 1997, Jennifer Coates, “The construction of a collaborative floor in women’s friendly talk”, in Talmy Givón, editor, Conversation: Cognitive, Communicative and Social Perspectives, page 72:
quote.text: Once all six friends are clear that the topic of Janet's story is a pub quiz, we launch into talk around this topic, combining factual information about quizzes we have participated in with fantasies about becoming a team ourselves.

definitions.definition: (education) A school examination of less importance, or of greater brevity, than others given in the same course.

quote.citation: 2015 May 18, Matt Farrell, Shannon Maheu, “Why open-book tests deserve a place in your courses”, in Faculty Focus‎[3]:
quote.text: For many it is hard to envision a scenario where a student completes an online quiz (or test) without using their smartphone, tablet, or other device to look up the answers, or ‘share’ those answers with other students.

definitions.definition: (transitive, archaic) To hoax; to chaff or mock with pretended seriousness of discourse; to make sport of, as by obscure questions.

quote.citation: 1850, William Makepeace Thackeray, The History of Pendennis‎[4]:
quote.text: he quizzed unmercifully all the men in the room—

quote.citation: 1863, Sheridan Le Fanu, The House by the Churchyard:
quote.text: 'Now, Puddock, back him up—encourage your man,' said Devereux, who took a perverse pleasure in joking; 'tell him to flay the lump, splat him, divide him, and cut him in two pieces—'It was a custom of the corps to quiz Puddock about his cookery  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive, archaic) To peer at; to eye suspiciously or mockingly.

quote.citation: 2023 August 31, “What's on in the Lords 4-7 September”, in UK Parliament‎[5]:
quote.text: This week members return to the chamber to quiz the government on the Zimbabwe election, teacher shortages, backlog of asylum applications and improving the system for dementia diagnosis.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To instruct (someone) by means of a quiz.
(transitive, obsolete, rare) To play with a quiz. (Can we add an example for this sense?)
